script.base: Denver is favored by 6.5 with implied totals DEN 25.0 / WAS 18.5 and Jayden Daniels out, so Denver should lead by halftime without a true blowout. Denver leans Dobbins late (33 of 64 listed rushes in weeks 9-11) while still throwing: Franklin was the target leader (27) in that same window. Washington's backup trails, check-downs and abandon-run risk rise, but the 18.5 team total caps yardage.
script.flip1: Washington's backup steals an early lead or hangs within one score. Denver passes more, Dobbins's late carry spike dies, Franklin and Harvey usage rises, and Washington can keep splitting Rodriguez (33/160) and Croskey-Merritt (32/96) instead of abandoning the run.
script.flip2: Denver is up big by halftime and clocks it. Starters are not a 10-point blowout risk at 6.5, but an extreme lead cuts Franklin's deep shots and Harvey's late snaps, and Washington's backs lose carries once they throw to chase.

injury_fallout: Official pre-kick report, not final inactives: Jayden Daniels Out (elbow) removes Washington's starter and his weeks 9-11 rush share (10/51); no backup QB is named in the pack, so Samuel/Ertz/Lane form is Daniels-era and suspect. Noah Brown Out (groin) is already absent from the weeks 9-11 target list, so no new redistribution versus recent usage. Chris Moore Questionable (illness) — if he sits, his 5 targets / 28 yards in that window tilt to Samuel (19) and Ertz (17); do not bet Moore. Will Harris Questionable (ankle) would help Denver deep shots only if inactive; not confirmed. Drake Jackson Out (knee) weakens Washington's edge, which helps Denver time-to-throw and rushing efficiency. Jonah Elliss Out (hamstring) slightly softens Denver's front/pressure (season blitz 32%). Nate Adkins Out (knee) is a non-target TE; Engram (13 targets) stays the receiving TE. Tyler Ott Out is a long snapper only. Sources: nflverse injury report in the pack; usage from weeks 9-11 logs.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone chart in the pack (coverage step limited). Proxy is location YPA: WAS allows left 8.75 (130 att), middle 9.39 (51), right 8.85 (146). DEN allows left 4.83 (140), middle 7.9 (70), right 7.0 (159).
matchup.pressure: WAS blitzes 28%; DEN EPA/dropback is +0.23 vs blitz and +0.01 vs none, so Washington pressure has been a Denver green light. DEN blitzes 32%; WAS EPA is +0.14 vs blitz and +0.05 vs none, but that is Daniels-era and he is out. Jackson out should lower WAS pressure; Elliss out should lower DEN pressure.
matchup.bleeds: WAS bleeds on the ground (4.93 YPC, 42 runs of 10+ in 11 games) and through the air at every landmark, worst in the middle (9.39), with 38 marked 20+ pass plays. DEN stuffs the run (3.67 YPC, only 11 runs of 10+) and the left side (4.83 YPA) but gives up the middle (7.9).
matchup.overlap: Franklin is the primary target (27 of 89 listed DEN targets, 541 air yards) into a WAS secondary that allows 8.75-9.39 YPA and explosives. Harvey is the overlap underneath: 11 targets, 80 yards, only 4 air yards, into that same middle leak plus a 4.93 YPC run defense. Washington's top options (Samuel 19 targets / 50 air, Ertz 17/216) would attack DEN's middle, but Daniels out breaks that sample.

pro_edge.script_read: Total 43.5 is middling, not a shootout and not a slog. Spread 6.5 is past the 3.5 dog-throws threshold, so Washington WR/TE/RB targets should rise if they trail, but Daniels out plus a 3.67 YPC Denver run defense caps conversion into yards. Denver as leader runs late, which supports the lead back's carries and puts starter snaps at risk only if the lead becomes a blowout (not the base 6.5). Build usage from shares: Franklin ~30% of listed targets, Harvey ~27% of non-QB rushes plus 11 targets, Dobbins ~52% of rushes.
pro_edge.best_price: No two-sided prices saved on any prop (Franklin 40.5, Harvey rush+rec 30.5, Dobbins 78.5, Sutton 61.5, Ertz 38.5, Samuel 42.5, Croskey-Merritt 33.5, Rodriguez 27.5, and the rest). Anchor no-vig N/A. Pinnacle/Circa/BetOnline not in the pack. No book, price, or timestamp to shop. Alt no-vig cannot be built. No stake: gate needs model p to beat no-vig by 3+ and that comparison cannot run.

edge_players.kills_it: Repeat of the 18-yard rush+rec game: checkdowns go to Engram (13 targets) or Badie, and Dobbins (33 carries) plus Nix (8) take the rush. A true blowout that benches him late also kills it.

data_check.notes: No sims, no projection file, no Pinnacle/Circa no-vig, and every main line is 'no price', so step 8 cannot compare model p to a sharp anchor or apply the 3-point gate. Available logs agree with both kept legs on central tendency: Harvey 3 of 4 and a 41-yard weeks 9-11 pace versus 30.5; Franklin mean 60 / three-game pace ~50 versus 40.5. Franklin's 2-of-4 rung rate and 5.6 yards per target are the disagreeing piece, so that lean is not sized. Dropped, not flagged as legs: Dobbins rush over 78.5 is the textbook lead-back plus 4.93 YPC spot, but it is only a lean and weeks 9-11 (138 yards, ~11 carries a game) disagree with 78.5 while last4 (81, 111, 61, 77) is 2-2, so step 8 drops it. Croskey-Merritt rush under 33.5 has last4 support (25, 38, 30, 28) and faces a 3.67 YPC defense, but the counter is as strong as the read: 3.67 times his ~11-carry rate lands near 40, Daniels's 10 rushes may spill to the committee, Elliss is out, and 32 yards a game is only 1.5 under 33.5, so step 10 drops it. Sutton under 61.5 and Samuel under 42.5 fight WAS/DEN location leaks or a Daniels-era sample. Ertz over 38.5 dies on the QB change. Mims, Lane, Moore, Rodriguez not used (zeros, committee variance, Moore questionable, or DEN run defense). Treat any mental 70% as invalid; stated model_p values are log hit-rates shrunk under 0.70, not sim outputs.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost because Washington's uncharted shell took away Franklin's 20-air-yard shots and he posted another 27-yard incompletion game while Denver, once ahead, fed Dobbins (the 33-carry back) and never needed nine Franklin targets. Harvey repeated the 18-yard rush+rec miss: Engram and Badie took the checkdowns, Nix kept the scramble carries (8/45 in weeks 9-11), and one screen died. The 30.5 and 40.5 numbers may already be the sharp price — nothing in the pack shows otherwise. An unsaved outdoor night forecast, or Harris and Moore both playing, would not have saved a pure incompletion script.
slip_story: One story: Washington's defense bleeds (4.93 YPC, 8.75-9.39 YPA) and Denver's secondary usage from weeks 9-11 still clears soft lines in a 25-point team total. Stack Harvey rush+rec over 30.5 with Franklin rec yards over 40.5. Do not add a total under, a Dobbins-only clock-kill under on Denver pass-catchers, or any Washington over — Daniels is out and WAS is implied 18.5, so Samuel/Ertz/Lane overs need the opposite quarterback. Two legs, no TDs, one market per player.
